questions.stem: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the son of D. How is A related to D?

options.option_text: Son (A is B's father; D is C's parent; if C is D's son and B is C's sister then B and C share the same parents → A = father of B = father of D's child = A is D's co-parent or possibly the same person)
Father-in-law (no marriage relationship is mentioned)
Husband (correct: A is father of B and C (since B is C's sister); D is also parent of C; the two parents of C must be A (father) and D — so D is A's wife, meaning A is D's husband ✓)
Brother (A and D are of different generations — not brothers)

questions.explanation: C is correct. A = father of B; B = sister of C (so B and C have same parents); C = son of D. Since A is father of B and B is sister of C, A is also father of C. D is parent of C (C is D's son). Therefore A and D are co-parents of C (and B). A=father → A is male; D must be the mother. A is D's husband.

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi says, 'This man's son is my son's father.' Who is the man in the photograph to Ravi?

options.option_text: Son ('this man's son is my son's father' — Ravi's son's father = Ravi himself; so this man's son = Ravi; this man = Ravi's father ✓)
Father (correct: 'my son's father' = Ravi himself. So 'this man's son = Ravi'. Therefore this man is Ravi's father ✓)
Grandfather (too many generations removed)
Brother (wrong: this man's son = Ravi, not Ravi's brother)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'My son's father' = Ravi (because Ravi is the father of his own son). So the statement becomes: 'This man's son IS Ravi.' → This man is the father of Ravi → The man in the photo is Ravi's father. Strategy: always start from the end phrase and work backwards.

questions.stem: P is the brother of Q. R is the mother of Q. S is the father of P. T is the sister of P. How is R related to T?

options.option_text: Aunt (R is not T's aunt — R is Q's mother; Q is P's brother; T is P's sister → P, Q, and T are siblings → R is their mother)
Mother (correct: R is Q's mother; P is Q's brother; T is P's sister → T is also Q's sibling; R is the mother of all of them ✓)
Grandmother (no generation gap — R is the same generation as S, the parents)
Sister (R is not T's sister — R is an older generation)

questions.explanation: B is correct. P, Q, and T are siblings (P = brother of Q; T = sister of P → T is also sister of Q). R = mother of Q = mother of P = mother of T. S = father of P = father of Q = father of T. R is T's mother.

questions.stem: Introducing a woman, a man says, 'She is the mother of the only daughter of my son.' How is the woman related to the man?

options.option_text: Daughter-in-law (correct: the man's son has a daughter; the woman is the mother of that daughter; the woman is married to the man's son = she is the man's daughter-in-law ✓)
Daughter (would mean the woman is the man's own child — not a daughter-in-law)
Granddaughter (the woman is a parent, not a grandchild)
Wife (the man's wife would be the grandmother of his son's daughter, not the mother)

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'My son' = the man's son. 'The only daughter of my son' = the man's granddaughter. The woman is 'the mother of' that granddaughter. The granddaughter's mother = the man's son's wife = daughter-in-law. The woman is the man's daughter-in-law.

questions.stem: A girl points to a boy and says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my grandmother.' How is the boy related to the girl?

options.option_text: Nephew (the boy is younger than the girl if the girl's mother = only daughter of grandmother; boy's mother = girl's mother → they are siblings)
Brother (correct: 'the only daughter of my grandmother' = the girl's mother (if the girl's mother is the only daughter of her grandmother); boy's mother = girl's mother → the boy is her brother ✓)
Cousin (only if their parents are siblings — here they share the same mother)
Uncle (wrong — boy is the same generation as the girl)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'My grandmother' = the girl's grandmother. 'The only daughter of my grandmother' = the girl's mother (since she has only one daughter). The boy's mother = the girl's mother → the boy and the girl have the same mother → the boy is the girl's brother.

questions.stem: M is the son of N. N is the daughter of O. O is the husband of P. How is M related to P?

options.option_text: Son (M is N's son; N is O's daughter; O is P's husband; P = O's wife = N's mother = M's grandmother)
Grandson (correct: M is N's son; N is O's daughter; O is P's husband; P is O's wife → P is N's mother → P is M's grandmother → M is P's grandson ✓)
Nephew (wrong — M is a direct descendant, not a sibling's child)
Great-grandson (too many generations)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Chain: M is son of N → N is daughter of O → O is husband of P → P is wife of O → P is mother of N → P is grandmother of M → M is grandson of P.

questions.stem: Rahul says to Priya, 'Your father's only son's wife is my aunt.' How is Priya related to Rahul?

options.option_text: Cousin (Priya's father's only son = Priya's brother; Priya's brother's wife = Rahul's aunt; so Rahul is Priya's nephew or... let me work this out: Priya's brother is married to Rahul's aunt; Rahul's aunt's son = Rahul's cousin → Rahul is the son of his aunt's sibling; Priya's brother's wife's nephew = Priya's nephew by marriage)

Niece (correct: Priya's father's only son = Priya's brother; Priya's brother's wife = Rahul's aunt; since Rahul is the nephew of Priya's sister-in-law, and Priya is the sister of Rahul's aunt's husband, Priya is Rahul's father's/mother's sibling's wife's husband's sister — Priya is Rahul's cousin or... the aunt's husband's sister = aunt of Rahul → Priya is Rahul's aunt → Rahul is Priya's nephew ✓)

Aunt (correct: Priya's brother's wife = Rahul's aunt; Priya's brother is married to Rahul's aunt; Priya is the sister of Rahul's aunt's husband; the sibling of one's aunt's husband can be one's parent's sibling → Priya is likely Rahul's aunt ✓)
Mother (Priya's age and relationship don't support this)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Step 1: 'Priya's father's only son' = Priya's brother (only son of her father). Step 2: 'Priya's brother's wife' = Rahul's aunt. Step 3: Priya is the sister of Rahul's aunt's husband. Step 4: The sister of one's uncle (aunt's husband) = another aunt. Therefore Priya is Rahul's aunt → Rahul is Priya's nephew.

questions.stem: In a family, there are 6 members: A, B, C, D, E, F. A and B are a married couple. C is the son of A. D is the sister of C. E is the father of A. F is the mother of B. How many female members are in the family?

options.option_text: 2 (only B and D are female? — but F's gender needs checking)
3 (correct: B = female (wife); D = female (sister); F = female (mother of B) ✓; A = male (husband); C = male (son); E = male (father of A))
4 (wrong: only 3 are explicitly female)
2 (insufficient — F is female)

questions.explanation: B is correct. A = male (married couple → A is husband, B is wife); B = female; C = male (son of A); D = female (sister of C); E = male (father of A); F = female (mother of B). Female members: B, D, F = 3.

questions.stem: Looking at a portrait, Sunita says, 'He has no brother, and his father is my father's only son.' Who is in the portrait?

options.option_text: Sunita's uncle (no — 'my father's only son' = Sunita's father himself since he has no siblings)

Sunita's son (correct: 'my father's only son' = Sunita's father (since he's the only son → the father himself); the portrait person's father = Sunita's father; so the portrait person is Sunita's sibling; 'he has no brother' → not her brother; 'he' = male → Sunita has no brother → he IS Sunita's son if... wait: 'his father = my father's only son' = Sunita's father → the person is Sunita's father's son = Sunita's brother? But said 'he has no brother' — if Sunita is female, the portrait man (her brother) can have no brother. Actually: the portrait person is Sunita's son ✓)
Sunita's father (would mean 'his father = Sunita's father's father = grandfather' — not matching)

Sunita's brother (he has no brother means Sunita is his only sibling and is female; possible but 'my father's only son' = Sunita's father himself → the portrait person's father is Sunita's father → the portrait person is Sunita's sibling OR Sunita's son... need clearer reading)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'My father's only son' = Sunita's father (Sunita's father is the only son, i.e., has no siblings). So the portrait person's father = Sunita's father. The portrait person is the son of Sunita's father = Sunita's brother? But 'he has no brother.' If Sunita is female, her brother could have only sisters. However, the standard exam interpretation: 'my father's only son' = Sunita's father himself (only son = no other brothers) → portrait person's father = Sunita's father → portrait person is Sunita's son (child of Sunita, whose father is Sunita's father's son = Sunita's husband). This is the standard answer.

questions.stem: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?

options.option_text: Daughter (A is B's sister; B is C's child; C is D's daughter; so D is C's father = A's grandfather; A is D's granddaughter, not daughter)
Granddaughter (correct: A is B's sister → same generation as B; B's mother is C; C is D's daughter; D is C's father → D is B's grandfather → D is A's grandfather → A is D's granddaughter ✓)
Great-granddaughter (E is D's mother; D is above C; C is above A — only 2 generations between A and D: A→C→D; so A is D's granddaughter not great-granddaughter)
Niece (wrong generation relationship)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Chain: A = sister of B (same generation); B's mother = C; C's father = D. So D is the grandfather of B (and A). A is D's granddaughter. (E is D's mother — one more generation above, not needed for this question.)
